nodes.description: Biallelic germline GIPC3 variants cause recessive hearing loss. Reported homozygous alleles include missense changes across GH1, PDZ and GH2 regions, c.685dupG, p.Trp301* and c.226-1G>T. Loss of normal adaptor function is inferred from segregation, the splice assay and animal models; individual human alleles need not abolish protein expression. In particular, p.Trp301* removes only the last 12 amino acids, and the family reports do not directly measure the function of their patient missense proteins.

nodes.description: In Gipc3 knockout inner hair cells, the cuticular plate fails to flatten from a hemispherical structure into a disk and fails to acquire the normal rounded-rectangular outline. Its area is smaller and depth greater, with initially similar volume; volume later declines after P21.5. GIPC3-MYO6 coupling of the plate to apical junctions is a proposed force-transmission mechanism, not a direct measurement of force. The link from this defect to absent hearing remains unresolved.

meta.association: Biallelic pathogenic variants in GIPC3 cause DFNB15/DFNB72/DFNB95. GIPC3 was first implicated in two small families (Indian DFNB15, Dutch DFNB95) alongside the ahl5 mouse, and statistically significant linkage came from six large Pakistani DFNB72 families. An adjacent 19p locus, DFNB81, is genetically distinct and not caused by GIPC3. Across populations GIPC3 is a rare cause of recessive deafness, with one exception: a founder missense allele, c.245A>G (p.Asn82Ser), in the Chuvash population of Russia.

nodes.description: A naturally occurring PDZ-domain missense allele underlying the ahl5 hearing-loss locus and the jams1 audiogenic-seizure locus. Mice have moderate hearing impairment at 4 weeks that becomes profound by one year, disorganised stereocilia bundles, reduced transduction currents, immature inner hair cell potassium currents, and late degeneration of the organ of Corti and spiral ganglion. Transgenic wild-type Gipc3 restores hearing thresholds at the click, 8 kHz and 16 kHz stimuli. The juvenile audiogenic seizures have no counterpart reported in patients.

The IMPC global knockout, closer in kind to the truncating patient alleles. It is profoundly deaf by one month, with malformed cuticular plates, compressed hair bundles and disrupted inner hair cell junctions, but largely normal early transduction currents.

In ahl5 mice the organ of Corti and spiral ganglion are histologically normal at 8 weeks, but by 52 weeks the organ of Corti has degenerated from base towards apex and the spiral ganglion has lost many neurons, in parallel with progression of the hearing loss from high to low frequencies. Whether the same degeneration occurs in patients, most of whom have early non-progressive loss, is unknown.

nodes.description: GIPC3 is expressed in cochlear inner and outer hair cells and spiral ganglion neurons. In hair cells it starts out cytoplasmic and becomes concentrated in the cuticular plate and at apical cell junctions during postnatal development. It binds myosin VI (MYO6) directly, depends on MYO6 for its junctional localisation, and binds PDZ-binding motifs of cytoskeletal and junctional proteins including MYO18A. The proposed role is as an adaptor coupling MYO6 to the actin structures of the hair cell apex; the older hypothesis, from its punctate cytoplasmic staining, was a role in vesicle trafficking. The localization and binding experiments use mouse, chicken and heterologous expression systems. In the Black Swiss Gly115Arg mouse, cochlear GIPC3 protein was reduced by 82%; this mouse-allele measurement is not a protein assay of the human variants. Separate electrophysiology identifies altered presynaptic calcium signaling. A later siRNA study proposes an additional mitochondrial role in cultured auditory cells and cochlear explants.
